limits: All five jobs completed successfully in the final attempt; this artifact audit certifies only the headless current frame clock lane (37 checks in eight loop paces).

The preceding-host control (29 cadence failures) and the three retained sabotages remain local evidence; this audit only shows that every check they fail passes in the hosted run (three of them under the names the review gave them). The C++ unit test (14 cases) runs through the test:runtime step. The first hosted run of the pull request failed two checks that assumed a loop timing the runner did not deliver; the checks were removed or rewritten in the review commits and this run is the first push of main on the revised head.
Bundle hashes and the native host hash are declared by the runner; no bundle or native binary is included in the artifact.
CI host hash is not required to equal the local built host.
Mobile and parity jobs are separate: only their PASSED markers are recorded, their outputs are not audited here.
Git-tree verification establishes tracked content at the pushed main checkout; it does not independently inspect a compiled native binary.
The slice's own committed limits are unchanged and still apply:

Timers (setTimeout, setInterval) still run on every Godot frame: they are not quantized to ticks, as RN's iOS and Android timers are quantized to display frames. The baseline check 'A zero-delay interval fires once on every Godot frame, tick or not' records it.

A Presentation tick carries the CPU time of its Godot frame, so the steps between ticks are as uneven as those frames and a decay lands lower than at a regular cadence (the presentation-bimodal lane ends about 1 px short of the Time lanes); the iOS display link hands RN the regular targetTimestamp, which is not implemented.
ADAPTIVE and MAILBOX V-Sync are mapped by detect_pacing and covered by the unit test only: the Compatibility renderer of this Mac reads both back as ENABLED.

Real displays are not certified: the lanes are headless and state V-Sync presentation and the refresh rate through validation seams; the headed observations are one exploratory run each on one 120 Hz Mac, outside the receipt.
Variable refresh rates, external screens, OS suspend and resume, behavior under JS load, frame budgets (GF-30) and Godot Android and iOS exports are not covered.
The clock has no visual output: there is no example scene and no capture.
No whole GF, checkpoint, dependency, weight or denominator closed: GF-05 and GF-19 are not at their first slice, so their slice checkpoints, already closed, do not change.

A window that cannot draw is detected from DisplayServer.window_can_draw (after review): only a minimized window was forced on purpose, and the OS reported false unprompted in other headed runs (the first seconds, or the middle of a run); occlusion by other windows was not exercised in a controlled way.
